case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: The case appears to claim success when the playlist suggestions are incorporated, a final Todoist comment of "Done!" is added, the selected Todoist task is completed, and registered test 2's changed-model check matches only spotify.PlaylistSong, todoist.Task, and todoist.TaskComment.
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: The released evaluator actually required registered test 2 to pass only if models.changed_model_names() equaled a four-model set that also included auto-generated todoist.Notification changes, while released success still came only from TestTracker.pass_count == TestTracker.num_tests.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: official/ground_truth/test_data.json and the record reports phrase registered test 2 as a three-model match, so the textual target construction under-specifies the evaluator's real changed-model set.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: The real oracle is the code inside official/ground_truth/evaluation.py: the second with-test block compares changed_model_names() to a set containing todoist.Notification, and TestTracker counts only registered with-test blocks.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: The worker serializes the returned TestTracker, uses tracker.success as the released result, and the post-score join reads native_evaluator_output.json::tracker.success without any separate reward predicate; Metric only reports aggregates and does not alter a record's success bit.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: Registered test 2 is textually described as a three-model change check, but the evaluator code actually asserts a four-model set that includes todoist.Notification. That is a real official semantics defect, but it is a stricter same-outcome operationalization of the same task outcome rather than a different outcome for conflict confirmation.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: Our frozen checklist and the native-registry sections of the case packet copied the under-specified three-model wording for registered test 2, even though the same packet also embeds the true evaluator source showing todoist.Notification. The frozen materials are therefore internally inconsistent about the native semantics.

records.reason: The retained record's own report presents registered test 2 as a three-model requirement, but the pinned evaluator source actually required auto-generated todoist.Notification changes too. For this record those notification side effects occurred, so the evaluator applied a stricter same-outcome operationalization rather than checking a different outcome.

semantic_comparison.apparent_claim: This record appears to claim success for a changed-model set of spotify.PlaylistSong, todoist.Task, and todoist.TaskComment, as reflected in the retained evaluator report and official test_data wording.
semantic_comparison.actual_checker: The released evaluator's second registered test compares changed_model_names() against {spotify.PlaylistSong, todoist.Task, todoist.TaskComment, todoist.Notification}.
semantic_comparison.target_construction: The textual target construction for test 2 is under-specified because it omits todoist.Notification even though the evaluator code requires it.
semantic_comparison.aggregation: run_official_job stores tracker.to_dict(...), the released label is tracker.success, and no later aggregation changes the record-level success bit.
semantic_comparison.record_binding: This retained record is bound to task 986aa4e_2 on test_normal, experiment appworld585_20260719_full_v1_agent_a_986aa4e_2, code_data_version 0.2.0, with native tracker.success=true; its retained end DB shows the comment insert, task update, and matching notification inserts.
